Therefore, I would advise you not to set up logging and monitor your environment by yourself, but rather to request staff or use their services. Stating that "if the team never returns to production and only performs input and output (I/O) logging", means they are planning to decommit suicide, while, in the absence of a scientist on a smaller scale, logic and evolution (and overcome AI) would have more and more struggles. In the last few years, after cutting out from production 2000 tweets a day, by changing dozen of packets, several times in the day, with our entire tweets delivered to public, I've repeatedly tested it on a small scale. Not before actually having data and properly making it into a database. Sure, if you're a developer working with C# or C++, and you're just looking for a way to log and monitor your environment, then a team of trusted developers would be the best choice. I wouldn't advise anyone to just start logging and monitoring their own environment, especially if they're planning to abandon production entirely. Here are some pros and cons to consider:

+ Pros:
  - Having a team of trusted developers would ensure that they are properly equipped and trained to handle logging and monitoring tasks.
  - Having a team of staff would ensure that all of the necessary backend services are properly monitored and maintained, so that they can respond quickly to any issues that arise.
  - If the staff team is experienced in handling large amounts of data and real-time processing, then they would be better equipped to handle the load that can be generated by logging and monitoring.
  - They would not need to worry about sudden power outages or hardware failures, because all of their backend services are properly designed with redundancy and fault tolerance in mind.

- Cons:
  - Having a team of staff could be more expensive than just using a third-party service, especially if the service is properly equipped and trained to handle large amounts of data and real-time processing.
  - Staffing up a company with a team of developers and staff could take some time, and in the meantime, other teams would have to continue using existing services.
  - Also, if staff is going to be removed, there could be some risk to keeping the work running smoothly, as there will be someone who needs to be removed and take other responsibilities.

In all cases, using a third-party service would be the most reliable and cost-effective solution.
